passage:
Simran, sit. You said you're doing all the work at the studio for less credit. Let me tell you about my first business. I'm Maria. At twenty-five I ran a small bakery with my partner Imran. Every dawn shift was mine, every invoice was mine, but the sign outside had his name in bigger letters. I was afraid, because it was my dream too.

One night I wrote it down: the hours I worked and the hours he did. I showed him. "This isn't fair, and I want the fix in writing: equal pay, or I cut my hours." He argued, then agreed for two months, then slid back. I had already spoken to a baker who offered me a job. I walked away.

I'm not telling you this to scare you. Say the imbalance out loud, write a fair fix, and be ready to leave.

qa.q: What did Maria write down one night?
qa.a: Maria wrote down the hours Maria worked and the hours Imran did.

qa.q: Why was Maria afraid to push back?
qa.a: Because the bakery was Maria's dream too, and Maria feared losing it.

qa.q: What steps did Maria take about the imbalance?
qa.a: Maria named the imbalance, asked in writing for equal pay or fewer hours, and prepared to leave when things slid back.

qa.q: How might Imran have seen Maria's demand?
qa.a: Imran argued at first and only agreed for two months, suggesting he felt challenged and may not have grasped how unbalanced the load was.

grounding: A partner keeps making Maria carry more work for less credit or pay; Maria states the imbalance, proposes a written fix and prepares to walk away.

passage:
Monday night.

Another client call I ran alone. Another invoice Pooja sent in her name. We started this design studio as equals, fifty-fifty. Now I do all the client work and the late nights, and Pooja "handles strategy", which as far as I can tell means lunch meetings and our shared social media page.

I counted this month: I billed 140 hours. She billed 30. We took home the same.

I feel used. And scared, because this studio is my whole life, and if I push, it might fall apart.

But I'm Ganga, and I didn't leave my old job to become someone's unpaid assistant.

So tomorrow I'll say it plainly: "The work split is 80-20 and the pay is 50-50. That isn't fair." I've written a one-page proposal: pay linked to hours, both our names on client work. If she won't discuss it by the end of the month, I'll talk to a lawyer about leaving.

My hands are shaking writing that. But it's written.

qa.q: How many hours did Ganga bill this month?
What was Ganga feeling as she wrote this entry?
qa.a: Ganga felt used and scared, afraid that pushing back might make the studio fall apart.

qa.q: What is Ganga's plan, and why is it a strong one?
qa.a: To name the imbalance plainly, propose a written fix, and be ready to leave with a lawyer's help if nothing changes, so Ganga isn't stuck being taken advantage of.

qa.q: How might Pooja see the studio's work split?
qa.a: Pooja may believe her strategy work is equally valuable and not notice how uneven the hours have become.

grounding: A diary entry shows someone whose business partner makes them carry more work for the same pay, who states the imbalance, proposes a written fix and prepares to walk away.

passage:
Yash: Mohit, can we talk about the split before the investor call?
Mohit: sure what's up
Yash: for 6 months I've done the product, support and the hiring. you've done the pitch decks
Yash: and in every deck it's "Mohit's company"
Mohit: come on, that's just how pitches work 😅
Yash: I get that. but I also haven't taken a salary since March and you have
Yash: I feel used, honestly. and I've been scared to say it because I don't want to lose this
Mohit: wow. ok. I didn't know you felt that way
Yash: I've written a proposal. equal salaries, my name on the deck as co-founder, and a written role split. sent to your email
Mohit: and if I don't agree?
Yash: then I think I have to step away. I don't want to, but I will
Mohit: ok. give me till Friday. I'll read it properly
Yash: thank you 🙏

qa.q: Since when has Yash not taken a salary?
qa.a: Yash hasn't taken a salary since March.

qa.q: How does Yash describe feeling about the arrangement?
qa.a: Yash feels used, and scared to speak up for fear of losing the venture.

qa.q: Why was Yash's approach a strong one?
qa.a: Yash stated the imbalance plainly, offered a written fix, and was honest about stepping away if nothing changed.

qa.q: How does Mohit react to Yash's message?
qa.a: Mohit is surprised and a little defensive at first, then agrees to read the proposal properly by Friday.

grounding: A chat shows someone whose partner leaves them carrying more work for less credit and pay, who states the imbalance, proposes a written fix and is ready to walk away if nothing changes.
